transcript: Yesterday I saw Covenant, a fantastic new play by York Walker, currently running at Roundabouts Underground Black Box set in Georgia in 1936. We follow five characters who all long for freedom and salvation in the religious sense, but more so from their shame and inner turmoil. Everyone has their secrets, and the way this play unfolds, I thought, was quite gripping, being so tightly constructed and performed. No scene is wasted and every character is so specific. It's also genuinely spooky, brought to life by the intimate nature of the space and the immediacy of the performances. The physical closeness really contributes to the energy of the piece, and it leaves you feeling a little claustrophobic at times, which I found very effective. I believe Covenant is technically sold out at this point, but roundabout offers some stand by seats, so keep an eye out if you can with that. Another program for my collection.
